name: WENO5-Z with q = 2, finite-difference flux form
source: Borges, Carmona, Costa and Don, J. Comput. Phys. 227 (2008), with the power q = 2 (the paper calls it p); not accessed by us, statements from secondary sources (arXiv 2004.07954 sec. 2.2, arXiv 2110.13607 sec. 2.2, R. Borges, PhD thesis, UFRJ 2014, p. 70): with q = 2 the scheme is fifth order at first-order critical points (eps = 1e-40). The square needs no absolute value: tau_5^2 = (beta_0 - beta_2)^2

claims.why: Borges et al. (secondary sources): q = 2 recovers fifth order at n_cp = 1. Sketch: (tau/beta_k)^2 = O(dx^2) with a common leading term c^2 dx^2, so omega_k - d_k = O(dx^3) at both stencils
the linear part has a non-zero dx^5 term at f' = 0
the thesis (p. 70): 'at critical points of order 2, all three schemes lose accuracy' (q = 2, eps = 1e-40); not derived
